solution: Factor every number into its distinct prime factors using a smallest-prime-factor sieve. Maintain a sliding window with two pointers and counts of how many elements contribute each prime; expand the right endpoint and move the left endpoint while the union contains more than k primes. Every valid window ending at the right endpoint is no longer than the maintained window, so recording its maximum length yields the optimum. The complexity is O(M log log M + nF) time and O(M + P) space, where M is the maximum value, F is the total number of distinct prime factors processed, and P is the number of tracked primes.

dropped.label: binary-search-answer
dropped.why: The direct linear sliding-window solution is the intended technique; binary-searching the length is an unnecessary alternative and the feasibility test is not the core idea.

added.label: prime-factorization
added.why: Factoring every array value into its distinct prime factors is an essential part of the solution, enabled by the SPF sieve.

notes: Binary-search-answer is a genuine alternative: feasibility for a fixed length can be checked with a fixed-size sliding window, and feasibility is monotone in the length.
